app.title: Product name. Do not translate.
titleBar.minimize: Tooltip of the window's minimize button. Use the wording Windows uses in your language.
titleBar.maximize: Tooltip of the window's maximize button. Use the wording Windows uses in your language.
titleBar.restore: Tooltip of the maximize button while the window is maximized. Use the wording Windows uses in your language.
titleBar.close: Tooltip of the window's close button. Closing keeps Aemeath running in the notification area.
titleBar.statusAria: Screen reader label of the status chips in the title bar.
chip.engineRunning: Title bar chip: the audio engine process is running.
chip.engineConnecting: Title bar chip: the app is waiting for the audio engine process to start.
chip.engineUnresponsive: Title bar chip: the audio engine stopped answering; it will be restarted automatically.
chip.engineVersionMismatch: Title bar chip: the engine and the app come from different Aemeath versions.
chip.offline: Title bar chip. {n} is the number of nodes whose device is offline.
chip.slots: Title bar chip. {used} is the number of virtual device slots in use, out of 16.
chip.slotsTip: Tooltip of the slots chip. {version} is the usbip-win2 driver version, e.g. 0.9.8.1.
chip.slotsTipNoDriver: Tooltip of the slots chip when the usbip-win2 command-line tool can't be found.
chip.rate: Title bar chip showing the engine sample rate. {rate} is a number such as 48.
chip.rateTip: Tooltip of the sample rate chip: clicking it opens the dialog.
chip.clock: Title bar chip naming the clock master. {name} is the node name.
chip.clockTip: Tooltip of the clock master chip. {name} is the node name; clicking opens Settings.
chip.rateSwitching: Shown instead of the sample rate while the engine switches to a new rate.
nav.aria: Screen reader label of the navigation rail.
nav.workbench: Navigation item and page title: the graph where nodes are connected.
nav.devices: Navigation item and page title: the list of virtual device slots.
nav.settings: Navigation item and page title: application settings.
nav.apps: Navigation item and page title: apps that are playing sound, and where their sound goes.
nav.tools: Navigation item and page title: small helpers that change Windows settings.
apps.sub: Introduction of the Apps page. 'Landing' is a defined term: the device an app's sound actually plays to.
apps.now: Small label above the device an app is playing to right now.
apps.followSystem: Landing choice: no per-app choice, the app follows the Windows default device.
apps.virtualInput: Landing choice for a virtual input. {node} is the node name, {device} the Windows device name.
apps.exclusive: A device that can't be chosen because Aemeath uses it exclusively. {name} is the device name.
apps.landingAria: Accessible name of the landing list. {app} is the app name.
apps.system: Name of the Windows system sounds session.
apps.systemHint: Shown instead of a hint for the system sounds row.
apps.restart: Shown when the app keeps playing to the old device after a new landing was chosen.
apps.assigning: Shown under the landing dropdown while Windows applies the new landing for this app.
apps.windowsSettings: Link under the page description that opens the Windows volume mixer settings, where users can pick an output device per app.
apps.unknownDevice: Current landing when the device name isn't known.
apps.empty: Shown when no app has an audio session.
apps.unavailable: Shown when the sessions can't be read.
apps.note: Note at the bottom of the Apps page about how per-app choices behave.
tools.default: Label of the list: the Windows default device.
tools.communications: Label of the list: the Windows default communication device.
tools.none: Shown when Windows has no default device of this kind.
tools.exclusive: A device that can't be chosen because Aemeath uses it exclusively. {name} is the device name.
tools.unavailable: Shown when the devices can't be read.
kind.externalInput: Node type: a recording device that exists on the PC independently of Aemeath (e.g. a microphone).
kind.virtualInput: Node type: one of Aemeath's virtual playback devices that apps play into.
kind.virtualOutput: Node type: one of Aemeath's virtual recording devices that apps such as OBS record from.
kind.externalOutput: Node type: a playback device that exists on the PC independently of Aemeath (e.g. headphones).
kind.bus: Node type: sums its inputs and sends them on.
wb.hint: Short help text in the workbench header.
wb.add: Button that opens the Add node dialog.
wb.fit: Button that zooms the workbench so that every node is visible.
wb.undo: Button that undoes the last change on the workbench.
wb.zoom: Current zoom level of the workbench. {percent} is a number such as 100.
node.aria: Screen reader label of a node. {kind} is the node type, {name} its name.
node.clockMaster: Tooltip of the clock icon on the node that is the clock master.
node.slotName: Fixed English device name of a virtual slot, e.g. 'Aemeath In 1'. Usually keep as is.
node.directionIn: Part of the fixed device name 'Aemeath In N'. Usually keep as is.
node.directionOut: Part of the fixed device name 'Aemeath Out N'. Usually keep as is.
node.pending: Status line of a node whose device is still being prepared.
node.rename: Tooltip for renaming a node by double-clicking its name. {name} is the current name.
node.offline.waitingForDevice: Status line of a node whose device is missing or can't be opened.
node.offline.inUseByOtherApp: Status line of a node whose device can't be opened because another program is using it (exclusively, or at all when Aemeath wants it exclusively).
node.offline.noSignal: Status line of a node whose device stopped delivering audio.
node.offline.slotRepairing: Status line of a virtual node whose virtual device is being re-attached.
node.offline.slotFailing: Status line of a virtual node whose virtual device failed to attach several times.
route.off: Label of a route that is turned off. {gain} is its gain, e.g. '−3 dB'.
route.toggle: Screen reader label of the on/off dot on a route label. {src} and {dst} are node names.
route.select: Screen reader label of a route label. {state} is 'on' or 'off', {gain} e.g. '−3 dB'.
route.stateOn: Inserted into route.select: the route is on.
route.stateOff: Inserted into route.select: the route is off.
route.moveHint: Tooltip of a route label: scrolling changes the gain, dragging (or Alt+arrow keys) slides the label along its route.
drag.hint: Tooltip next to the pointer while dragging a new route.
drag.ok: Tooltip while dragging a new route over a node it can connect to. {dst} is the node name.
drag.selfRoute: Tooltip while dragging a route back onto the node it started from.
drag.duplicate: Tooltip while dragging a route that already exists.
drag.loop: Tooltip while dragging a route that would send the sound in a circle.
drag.noInput: Tooltip while dragging onto an input node, which can't receive sound. {dst} is the node name.
drag.noOutput: Tooltip while dragging onto an output node, which can't send sound. {dst} is the node name.
toast.routeDeleted: Notification after deleting a route. {src} and {dst} are node names.
toast.nodeDeleting: Notification shown while a node is being deleted, replaced by the result when it finishes.
toast.nodeDeleted: Notification after deleting a node. {name} is the node name.
toast.deviceReplaced: Notification when a device came back with a new ID (for example plugged into another USB port) and Aemeath switched the node to it. {node} is the node name, {device} the device name.
toast.undo: Button in the notification that restores what was deleted.
toast.dismiss: Screen reader label of the button that closes a notification.
error.unavailable: Error: the app's background part is not running.
error.invalidName: Error: a node name is empty or longer than 64 characters.
error.routeRejected: Error: a route can't be created.
error.noFreeSlot: Error: all eight virtual devices of one direction are already used.
error.slotOccupied: Error: the chosen virtual device is used by another node.
error.deviceInUse: Error: there is already a node for this device.
error.notFound: Error: the node or route was removed in the meantime.
error.failed: Generic error. {message} is an English technical message.
add.title: Title of the Add node dialog.
add.kind: Label of the node type choice in the Add node dialog.
add.device: Label of the device list in the Add node dialog.
add.noDevices: Shown in the Add node dialog when there is no device to choose.
add.loadingDevices: Shown in the Add node dialog while the device list loads.
add.name: Label of the node name field in the Add node dialog.
add.cancel: Button that closes the Add node dialog without adding.
add.kindHint.externalInput: Explanation under the External input choice.
add.kindHint.virtualInput: Explanation under the Virtual input choice.
add.kindHint.bus: Explanation under the Bus choice. A bus is an internal mixing node with no device.
add.kindHint.virtualOutput: Explanation under the Virtual output choice.
add.kindHint.externalOutput: Explanation under the External output choice.
dev.sub: Introduction at the top of the Devices page.
dev.driverVal: Summary value. {version} is the driver version.
dev.driverMissing: Summary value when the driver's command-line tool can't be found.
dev.driverUntested: Shown under the driver version when the installed usbip-win2 is newer than the version Aemeath ships and was tested with.
dev.health: Summary heading: the periodic check that virtual devices are attached.
dev.healthOk: Summary value: all occupied slots are attached.
dev.healthWaiting: Summary value: the engine isn't running yet.
dev.healthFix: Summary value. {n} is the number of slots being re-attached.
dev.usage: Summary heading: how many slots are in use.
dev.usageVal: Summary value. {used} is the number of slots in use, out of 16.
dev.check: Button that checks every slot right away.
dev.inputs: Section heading for the eight virtual input slots.
dev.inputsSub: Explanation next to the virtual inputs heading.
dev.outputs: Section heading for the eight virtual output slots.
dev.outputsSub: Explanation next to the virtual outputs heading.
dev.colName: Column heading: the device's name as shown by Windows.
dev.colOcc: Column heading: the node that uses the slot.
dev.colState: Column heading: whether the device is plugged in.
dev.colFmt: Column heading: the sample rate and format Windows uses for the device.
dev.stOk: Slot status: plugged in and working.
dev.stOff: Slot status: unplugged because no node uses it.
dev.stSettling: Slot status: attached, waiting for Windows to show the device.
dev.stEngine: Slot status: the engine isn't running.
dev.stFix: Slot status while re-attaching. {n} is the attempt number.
dev.stFail: Slot status after several failed attempts. {n} is the attempt number.
dev.free: Occupied-by column when no node uses the slot.
dev.fmt: Device format. {rate} is e.g. 48, {format} e.g. '32-bit float'.
dev.fmtUnknown: Device format column when the format can't be read.
dev.fmtOff: Hint under the format of an unplugged slot.
dev.fmtSame: Hint under the format when it matches the engine.
dev.fmtDiff: Hint under the format when its sample rate differs from the engine.
dev.fmtMismatch: Hint under the format when it does not yet match the node's setting.
dev.edit: Small button in a slot row: opens the settings of the node that occupies the slot.
dev.note: Footnote at the bottom of the Devices page.
sampleFormat.int24In32: Audio sample format: 24-bit samples in 32-bit containers. Shown like 24-bit integer.
set.engineRate: Settings row title: the engine sample rate (glossary).
set.resampler: Settings row title: the resampler used by default.
set.clock: Settings row: which device the engine timeline follows.
set.clockSystem: Dropdown option: follow the system clock instead of a device.
set.detect: Settings group heading: finding and reconnecting audio devices.
set.detectSub: Explanation under the row: detection is automatic, the button only retries immediately.
set.ui: Settings group heading: the user interface.
set.langSys: Language choice: follow the Windows display language.
set.langZh: Language choice. Always written in Simplified Chinese.
set.langEn: Language choice. Always written in English.
reg.title: Title of the panel shown while the 16 virtual devices are set up on first start.
reg.failing: Warning in the setup panel. {slots} is a list such as 'In 3, Out 5'.
reg.waitingEngine: Shown in the setup panel while the engine isn't running.
tray.open: Notification area menu item that shows the window.
tray.quit: Notification area menu item that stops Aemeath completely, including the audio.
tray.redetect: Notification area menu item: try to open every offline device again now.
strip.gate: Label of the gate control on an input node: it mutes the input while the signal is below a threshold.
nodeSettings.title: Title of the node settings dialog. {name} is the node name.
nodeSettings.slot: Label of the list for choosing which virtual device slot the node uses.
nodeSettings.slotHint: Note under the slot list: each slot has its own fixed device name in Windows.
nodeSettings.gateOff: Value shown when the gate is turned off.
nodeSettings.gateHint: Explanation under the gate threshold slider.
nodeSettings.confirm: Button that applies the node settings.
nodeSettings.candidates: Heading of a box in node settings, shown when the node's device disappeared and several devices with its name exist.
nodeSettings.candidatesHint: Explanation in that box. {device} is the device name.
nodeSettings.useCandidate: Button that switches the node to the chosen device right away.
node.formatLine: Line on an online external device node. {rate} is the sample rate in kHz, {format} the sample format, {mode} is Exclusive or Shared.
node.exclusive: The {mode} value when Aemeath uses the device exclusively.
node.shared: The {mode} value when the device is shared with other apps.
node.redetect: Small button on an offline device node: try to open the device again now.
node.useShared: Small button on a node whose device can't be opened exclusively: switch the node to shared mode.
node.offline.exclusiveNotAllowed: Node state: the user turned off 'Allow applications to take exclusive control' in the Windows sound settings.
node.chooseDevice: Small button on an offline node when several devices with its device's name exist: opens node settings to choose one.
menu.redetect: Node menu item for external devices: try to open the device again now.
preset.title: Heading of the card shown on an empty workbench.
preset.body: Text of that card: what the preset adds.
preset.use: Button that adds the preset nodes.
preset.inputName: Name given to the preset's virtual input node (the user can rename it).
preset.outputName: Name given to the preset's virtual output node (the user can rename it).
device.exclusive: Checkbox in the add-node and node settings dialogs. Checked by default.
device.exclusiveHint: Explanation under the exclusive checkbox: what it does and what it costs.
device.formatLabel: Label of the list of device formats (sample rate and sample format) used in exclusive mode.
device.format: One device format. {rate} is in kHz, {format} is a sample format such as 32-bit integer.
device.recommended: First item of the format list when the recommended format isn't known yet.
device.recommendedFormat: First item of the format list. {format} is the recommended device format.
device.probing: Shown while Aemeath asks the device which formats it supports.
device.probeFailed: Shown when the supported formats can't be read.
device.buffer: Label of the buffer (device period) list in exclusive mode.
device.bufferDefault: Buffer choice. {ms} is the device's default period in milliseconds.
device.bufferDefaultUnknown: Buffer choice when the device's default period isn't known.
device.bufferMinimum: Buffer choice. {ms} is the device's minimum period in milliseconds.
device.bufferMinimumUnknown: Buffer choice when the device's minimum period isn't known.
device.bufferCustom: Buffer choice that shows a number box in milliseconds.
device.bufferMs: Accessible name of the custom buffer number box.
device.sharedHint: Shown instead of the format and buffer options in shared mode, when the current format isn't known.
device.sharedFormat: Shown instead of the format and buffer options in shared mode. {format} is the current Windows format.
device.resampler: Label of the per-node resampler list.
device.resamplerGlobal: First item of the resampler list: use the default from Settings.
device.resamplerGlobalHint: Explanation under the resampler list when the global default is used.
rate.title: Title of the engine sample rate dialog.
rate.label: Label of the sample rate list.
rate.body: What changing the engine sample rate does.
rate.recording: Warning when a recording is running.
rate.over384: Warning when the chosen rate is above what virtual devices support.
rate.apply: Button that applies the new sample rate.
slot.format: Label of the list that chooses how a virtual device's format is decided.
slot.follow: Choice: the virtual device follows the engine sample rate. Glossary term 'Follow Engine'.
slot.fixed: Choice: the user picks a sample rate and sample format.
slot.followHint: Note under the format list when following the engine.
slot.rate: Label of the sample rate list.
slot.sampleFormat: Label of the sample format list.
slot.sendTitle: Heading above the settings of an external insert's send side (glossary: Send).
slot.changeConfirm: Confirmation before changing the format of a virtual device that is online.
resampler.latency: One-line note under the resampler preset list. {ms} is the added latency in milliseconds, possibly written as <0.1.
resampler.polyWarning: Warning shown for the Poly Async algorithm: it distorts high frequencies and has no anti-aliasing.
resampler.preset.label: Label of the resampler preset list.
resampler.preset.polyAsync.fastest: Resampler preset: linear interpolation, the cheapest.
resampler.preset.polyAsync.fine: Resampler preset: quintic interpolation, the best of this algorithm.
resampler.preset.fftSync.lowLatency: Resampler preset: the shorter FFT block, about 8 ms of latency.
resampler.preset.fftSync.balanced: Resampler preset: the longer FFT block, about 32 ms of latency.
strip.aria: Accessible name of a console strip. {name} is the node name.
strip.gateAria: Accessible name of a strip's gate threshold slider.
strip.gainAria: Accessible name of a strip's gain fader.
strip.mute: Button on a strip that mutes the node. Keep it short: the strip is narrow.
strip.muteAria: Accessible name of the mute button.
strip.dragHint: Tooltip of a strip's title: the full node name, and that dragging reorders strips.
mx.title: Heading of the route matrix pane (a grid of sources × destinations).
mx.pinOnly: Switch that limits the matrix to nodes pinned to the console.
mx.from: Corner label for the rows (sources). Kept in English in both languages, like the prototype.
mx.to: Corner label for the columns (destinations). Kept in English in both languages.
mx.empty: Shown instead of the matrix when there are no sources or no destinations.
mx.off: Text in a matrix cell whose route exists but is off. Very short: the cell is 32 px wide.
mx.stOn: Route state in the matrix status line. {gain} is the send gain, e.g. −6 dB.
mx.stOff: Route state: the route exists but is turned off.
mx.stNone: Route state: there is no route.
mx.cell: Status line and accessible name of a matrix cell. {src} and {dst} are node names, {state} is one of the states.
mx.idle: Status line under the matrix when no cell is hovered.
mx.lgOn: Legend: a filled cell is a route that is on.
mx.lgOff: Legend: a dashed cell is a route that is off.
mx.lgNone: Legend: an empty cell has no route.
mx.lgKeys: Legend: mouse and keyboard actions on cells.
mx.newRoute: Context menu item on an empty matrix cell.
grp.in: Group heading in the matrix: input nodes.
grp.proc: Group heading in the matrix: processing nodes (buses).
grp.out: Group heading in the matrix: output nodes.
con.title: Heading of the console pane: vertical strips of pinned nodes.
con.caption: Caption next to the console heading. {n} is the number of pinned nodes.
con.pin: Button that opens a list of nodes to pin to the console.
con.allPinned: Disabled item in that list when every node is already pinned.
con.empty: Shown in the console when nothing is pinned.
menu.pin: Node menu item that adds the node to the console.
menu.unpin: Node menu item that removes the node from the console.
menu.setClock: Node menu item for external devices: make this device the clock master.
menu.clearClock: Node menu item: stop using this device as the clock master; the system clock is used instead.
menu.aria: Accessible name of the ⋯ button on a node. {name} is the node name.
menu.nodeSettings: Context menu item that opens the node settings dialog.
menu.rename: Context menu item that starts renaming the node in place.
menu.deleteNode: Context menu item that deletes the node (can be undone).
menu.routeOn: Context menu item on a route that is off.
menu.routeOff: Context menu item on a route that is on.
menu.resetGain: Context menu item that sets the route's send gain back to 0 dB.
menu.showLabel: Route menu item: shows the route's label (on/off dot and gain) on the workbench. Hidden by default.
menu.hideLabel: Route menu item: hides the route's label on the workbench.
menu.resetLabel: Route menu item: moves the route's gain label back to the middle of the route.
menu.deleteRoute: Context menu item that deletes the route (can be undone).
menu.addHere: Context menu item on empty workbench space: adds a node where you right-clicked.
menu.fit: Context menu item on empty workbench space: zooms so all nodes are visible.
chip.notRunning: Title bar chip. {n} is the number of app sources whose program is not running. Not a warning.
chip.notRunningTip: Tooltip of the 'not running' chip in the title bar.
kind.appSource: Node type: captures the sound of one program by its executable path.
node.notRunning: Status line on an app source node whose program is not running. Not an error.
node.notRunningHint: Tooltip on an app source that is not running. {program} is the file name of the executable.
node.programMissing: Warning on an app source: the file at the chosen path is gone, so Aemeath stopped looking for it.
node.chooseProgram: Button that opens a file picker to bind the app source to another executable.
error.programInUse: Error when adding a second app source node for the same executable.
error.invalidProgram: Error when the chosen path is not an absolute path to an .exe.
add.program: Label of the program picker for an app source.
add.programPlaceholder: Placeholder of the list of programs that are playing sound.
add.browse: Button that opens a file picker to choose an executable that isn't running.
add.programFilter: File type name in the file picker.
add.appSourceNote: Explains the two limits of app sources. 'Landing' is the device an app plays to.
add.kindHint.appSource: Hint under the 'App source' choice in the Add node dialog.
apps.addSource: Button on an app's card: creates an app source node for this program.
apps.showSource: Button on an app's card when this program already has an app source node.
node.duplicate: Warning: the app's own landing and its app source both reach the same destination, so the sound is doubled. {program} and {destination} are node names.
toast.landingRestored: Toast: Windows had changed this app's device; Aemeath restored the landing the user chose.
confirm.deleteLanding: Confirmation before deleting a node that apps are assigned to. {n} is the number of apps.
mx.lgDup: Legend of the route matrix: a route on a path that doubles an app's sound.
kind.externalInsert: Node type: sends its input to an external program (for example noise removal) and takes the result back.
add.kindHint.externalInsert: Hint under the 'External insert' choice in the Add node dialog.
add.returnDevice: Label of the device an external insert reads the processed sound from.
add.insertSend: {slot} is a virtual device name such as 'Aemeath Out 2'.
add.usedAsReturn: Shown after a device name when it can't be chosen: an external insert already reads from it. {node} is a node name.
add.usedByNode: Shown after a device name when it can't be chosen. {node} is a node name.
nodeSettings.insertHint: {device} is the Windows device name of the virtual device that carries the sound to the external program.
nodeSettings.copy: Button: copies the virtual device name to the clipboard.
nodeSettings.copyFailed: Toast when copying the device name fails.
kind.recorder: Node type: writes the sound routed into it to a file.
add.kindHint.recorder: Hint under the 'Recorder' choice in the Add node dialog.
chip.recording: Title bar chip. {n} is the number of recorder nodes that are recording.
node.record: Button on a recorder node that starts recording.
node.stopRecording: Button on a recorder node that stops recording.
toast.recordingFailed: Toast when a recording fails. {node} is a node name, {reason} the failure text.
rec.folder: Label of the folder where recordings are saved.
rec.chooseFolder: Button that opens a folder picker.
rec.openFolder: Button that opens the recording folder in File Explorer.
rec.folderHint: Note under the recording folder: changing it does not move old files.
rec.defaultFormat: Label of the recording file format.
rec.defaultDepth: Label of the recording bit depth.
rec.settingsHint: Hint under the recorder format settings.
rec.flacRateHint: Shown when FLAC is selected and the engine sample rate is above what FLAC recording supports.
rec.depth.float32: Bit depth option. Not available for FLAC.
rec.empty: Empty state of the Recordings page.
rec.failed.diskFull: State of a recorder node that stopped because the disk is full.
rec.failed.writeFailed: State of a recorder node that stopped because of a write error.
rec.startAria: Screen reader label of the record button. {name} is a node name.
rec.stopAria: Screen reader label of the stop button. {name} is a node name.
chip.panicMute: Title bar chip shown while the panic mute is on.
chip.panicMuteTip: Tooltip of the panic mute chip.
menu.hotkey: Context menu item on a route: opens a dialog to set its hotkey.
error.hotkeyModifierRequired: Error when a toggle hotkey has no modifier.
error.hotkeyToggleOnly: Error when choosing hold for an action that only toggles.
error.hotkeyConflict: {object} describes what the key is bound to, such as 'A1 Rear Mic · Mute'.
hotkey.global: Group heading on the Hotkeys page.
hotkey.dedicated: Group heading on the Hotkeys page: hotkeys that belong to a node or route.
hotkey.dedicatedEmpty: Empty state of the dedicated group.
hotkey.hint: Hint in the route hotkey dialog.
hotkey.pressKey: Hotkey field while waiting for a key.
hotkey.mode: Accessible name of the hotkey mode selector.
hotkey.toggle: Hotkey mode: each press flips the state.
hotkey.hold: Hotkey mode: the state is flipped only while the key is held.
hotkey.occupied: Shown when Windows refuses to register the hotkey.
hotkey.mouseX1: Name of a mouse side button.
hotkey.mouseX2: Name of a mouse side button.
hotkey.targetMute: Hotkey target. {node} is the node code and name.
hotkey.targetRecord: Hotkey target. {node} is the node code and name.
hotkey.targetRoute: Hotkey target. {from} and {to} are node codes.
hotkey.allRecording: Global hotkey action. If any recorder is recording, all stop; otherwise all start.
hotkey.recordLabel: Label in node settings of a recorder node.
set.data: Settings group heading: where Aemeath stores its data.
set.openData: Button: open the configuration folder in File Explorer.
set.openLogs: Button: open the log folder in File Explorer.
set.updateTitle: Status text before any check has run.
set.updateCurrent: Caption showing the installed version. {version} e.g. 0.1.0.
set.updateLatest: Status when there is no newer version.
set.updateAvailable: Status when a newer version exists. {version} e.g. 0.2.0.
set.updateReady: Status when the update is downloaded.
set.updateFailed: Status when the check or download failed.
set.updateNotes: Button: open the release notes of the new version in a browser.
set.updateReleases: Button: open the GitHub Releases page in a browser.
set.updateApply: Button: restart Aemeath to install the downloaded version.
set.updateRecording: Explains why updating is disabled during a recording.
set.updateOnStart: Setting: check for updates each time Aemeath starts.
set.startup: Settings group heading: how Aemeath starts.
set.autostart: Setting: launch Aemeath automatically when the user signs in to Windows.
set.crashSub: Explanation under the crash dump row.
set.crashEnable: Button that turns crash dumps on.
set.crashEnabled: Shown instead of the button when crash dumps are on.
set.removeDevices: Settings row title, portable version only.
set.removeAction: Confirm button of the removal dialog.
set.removeConfirm: Confirmation before removing the virtual devices.
set.themeMode: Settings row title: light or dark theme.
set.themeSystem: Choice: follow the Windows light or dark setting.
set.accent: Settings row title: the accent color.
set.accentCustom: Accessible name of the color picker.
set.accentReset: Button: back to the default accent color.
set.backgroundFilter: File type name in the file picker.
set.overlay: Settings row title: the overlay over the background image.
